mainTopic: Which תנא the משנה follows on a child's lineage, and how the words "כל מקום" and "ואיזו זו" include or exclude cases not on its list.
overview: The גמרא continues a challenge against the משנה's rule that wherever there is valid קידושין and no עבירה, the child follows the father. In רבי יוסי's view, a convert who marries a ממזרת does no wrong, yet the child is a ממזר. רבי יוחנן answers that the משנה follows רבי יהודה, who forbids that marriage, so the words "כל מקום" in the second clause include it. A second answer keeps the משנה like רבי יוסי and says the words "ואיזו זו" limit the first rule to the cases it lists. The גמרא then tests the list with more cases: a חלל who married a בת ישראל, an ישראל who married a חללה, the son of Egyptian converts, and רבין's report about converts from two nations. Each case is answered: by following רבי דוסתאי בן רבי יהודה, by the broad words "כל מקום", or by the limiting words "ואיזו זו". Finally the גמרא goes back and questions the רבי יוסי reading, showing how neatly every extra word fits if the משנה follows רבי יהודה.

steps.title: A convert who married a ממזרת seems to break the משנה's rule
steps.stepSummary: The challenge points to a convert married to a ממזרת: valid קידושין, no עבירה, yet the child is a ממזר. A ברייתא shows this is רבי יוסי's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is the case of a convert who married a ממזרת. There is valid קידושין and no sin, yet the child follows the flawed parent. As a ברייתא teaches: if a convert married a ממזרת, the child is a ממזר. These are the words of רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is challenging the משנה's rule that whenever there is קידושין and no עבירה, the child follows the father. Here is a case that seems to break it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי יוסי's view a convert is allowed to marry a ממזרת, so there is no עבירה. By the משנה's rule the child should follow the father, who is a convert and not flawed. Yet the ברייתא says the child is a ממזר, following the flawed mother.

keyTerms.meaning: A convert to Judaism
A female ממזר, born from a forbidden union
Halachically valid betrothal
A transgression; here, a forbidden marriage
The parent with the flawed lineage

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two rules of the משנה. With קידושין and no עבירה, the child follows the father. With קידושין and an עבירה, the child follows the flawed parent. This challenge only works if the marriage has no עבירה.

phrases.english: a convert who married a mamzeret,
where there is betrothal and there is no transgression,
yet the child follows the flawed parent,
as it is taught: a convert who married a mamzeret,
the child is a mamzer; these are the words of Rabbi Yosei!

steps.triggerLanguage: גֵּר שֶׁנָּשָׂא מַמְזֶרֶת, דְּיֵשׁ קִידּוּשִׁין וְאֵין עֲבֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a challenge against the משנה that began before this section.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that wherever there is קידושין and no עבירה, the child follows the father.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In רבי יוסי's view, a convert marrying a ממזרת involves no עבירה, yet the child follows the flawed mother.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording רבי יוסי's view that the child of a convert and a ממזרת is a ממזר.

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי יהודה, not רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the משנה follows רבי יהודה. In his view a convert may not marry a ממזרת, so there is an עבירה and the child rightly follows the flawed parent.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Do you think the משנה is רבי יוסי? The משנה is רבי יהודה. He says a convert may not marry a ממזרת, so there is קידושין and there is a sin, and the child follows the flawed parent.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers רבי שמעון by saying the משנה follows a different תנא, רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, this marriage is forbidden, so the case moves into the משנה's second rule: קידושין with an עבירה. Under that rule the child follows the flawed parent, so being a ממזר fits perfectly.

keyTerms.meaning: Do you really think...?
Our משנה
He may not marry

phrases.english: He said to him: Do you maintain
that the mishna follows Rabbi Yosei?
The mishna follows Rabbi Yehuda, who says:
A convert may not marry a mamzeret,
so there is betrothal and there is a transgression,
and the child follows the flawed parent.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי סָבְרַתְּ מַתְנִיתִין רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הִיא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the משנה to a different תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה follows רבי יוסי, so the convert's case breaks its rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows רבי יהודה. The case involves an עבירה and fits the second rule.

steps.title: Then the משנה should have listed this case
steps.stepSummary: If the convert-and-ממזרת case belongs under the second rule, why didn't the משנה name it as an example?
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let the משנה teach it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects to the answer: if this case fits the second rule, the משנה should have said so openly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists specific examples for its rules. Leaving out a case that supposedly belongs there looks odd.

keyTerms.meaning: Then let it teach it

phrases.english: But then let it teach it!
phrases.notes: Meaning: let the משנה list the convert and the ממזרת among its examples.

steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה, following רבי יהודה, covers the convert-and-ממזרת case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the case belongs to the second rule, the משנה should have stated it explicitly.

steps.title: The words "כל מקום" in the סיפא include it
steps.stepSummary: The משנה did include the case, through the broad wording "כל מקום" in its second clause.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה taught "כל מקום" (any case) in the second clause to include this case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה hinted at this case with general wording instead of naming it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "כל מקום" is wider than the listed examples. It adds other cases of קידושין with an עבירה, like a convert who married a ממזרת according to רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: Any case: wording that widens a rule
The latter clause of a משנה
To include

phrases.english: It taught "any case"
in the latter clause, to include it.
phrases.notes: The latter clause is the rule about קידושין with an עבירה, where the child follows the flawed parent.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading broad wording as including the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה never mentions the convert-and-ממזרת case.
steps.terutzMaskana: "כל מקום" in the סיפא includes it.
steps.whatToRemember: First approach: the משנה follows רבי יהודה. A convert marrying a ממזרת is קידושין with an עבירה, so the child follows the flawed parent, and "כל מקום" includes it.

steps.title: Second answer: the משנה follows רבי יוסי, and "ואיזו זו" limits the rule
steps.stepSummary: A second answer keeps the משנה like רבי יוסי. The phrase "ואיזו זו" limits the first rule to the cases the משנה lists, so the convert's case isn't covered.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: really, it is רבי יוסי, and the משנה taught "ואיזו זו" (which case is this?) to exclude other cases.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different answer to the original challenge from step 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the convert case does have no עבירה, as רבי יוסי holds. But "ואיזו זו" signals that the child follows the father only in the listed cases. So the convert case is excluded, and the child can be a ממזר.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say: introduces another answer
Actually; really
Which case is this?: introduces the list of cases
To exclude

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
Actually, it is Rabbi Yosei,
and it taught "which case is this" to exclude.
phrases.notes: These words open the משנה's list for the first rule, so only the listed cases count.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא לְעוֹלָם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative answer to step 1, instead of the approach in steps 2-4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading limiting wording as excluding the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the משנה follows רבי יוסי, the convert's case breaks the first rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: "ואיזו זו" limits the first rule to the listed cases, so the convert's case is not included.

steps.title: What about a חלל who married a בת ישראל?
steps.stepSummary: Is the list really complete? A חלל who married a בת ישראל has קידושין, no עבירה, and the child follows the father, yet it isn't listed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Only "which case is this" and nothing more? But there is a חלל who married a בת ישראל. There is קידושין and no sin, and the child follows the male!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that the משנה's list is complete. Here is another case that fits the first rule but is missing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חלל may marry a regular Jewish woman, so there is no עבירה. If the child follows the father and is a חלל, this case belongs in the list. That weakens the claim that the list is meant to be closed.

keyTerms.meaning: And nothing more?
A son of a כהן from a forbidden union, who loses כהונה status
A regular Jewish woman

phrases.english: "Which case is this", and no more?
But there is a halal who married an Israelite woman,
where there is betrothal and there is no transgression,
and the child follows the male!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second answer in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the cases listed after "ואיזו זו" are the only ones.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A חלל and a בת ישראל fit the first rule, yet are not listed.

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי דוסתאי בן רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: No problem: the משנה follows רבי דוסתאי בן רבי יהודה. In his view the child of a חלל and a בת ישראל is fully fit, so the case does not need to be listed.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not difficult. The משנה holds like רבי דוסתאי בן רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא removes the challenge by saying the משנה follows a תנא with a different view about the חלל's child.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי דוסתאי's view, the child of a חלל and a בת ישראל is fully fit. So the child does not follow the father's flawed status, and the case does not belong on the list. The list stays complete, and the second answer stands.

keyTerms.meaning: This is not difficult
He holds

steps.whatToRemember: Second approach: the משנה follows רבי יוסי, and "ואיזו זו" closes the list. A חלל's case is left out because the משנה holds like רבי דוסתאי בן רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: This is not difficult,

phrases.aramaic: כְּרַבִּי דּוֹסְתַּאי בֶּן רַבִּי יְהוּדָה סְבִירָא לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: for it holds like Rabbi Dostai ben Rabbi Yehuda.
phrases.notes: He holds that the child of a חלל and a regular Jewish woman is fully fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לָא קַשְׁיָא כְּרַבִּי דּוֹסְתַּאי בֶּן רַבִּי יְהוּדָה סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the משנה to a specific תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The child of a חלל and a בת ישראל follows the father, so the list is incomplete.
steps.terutzMaskana: Following רבי דוסתאי, that child is fully fit, so the case does not belong on the list.

steps.title: An Israelite who married a חללה is missing from the list
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points to another case that fits the first rule but is not listed: an ישראל who married a חללה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is the case of an ישראל who married a חללה. There is קידושין and no עבירה, and the child follows the father. Why isn't it listed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises one more case that seems to fit the משנה's first rule but is missing from its list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 7 the case of a חלל who married a בת ישראל was solved by saying the משנה follows רבי דוסתאי. Now the גמרא flips the genders: an ישראל who marries a חללה. That marriage is fully allowed, it works, and the child follows the father and is a regular ישראל. So it fits the first rule perfectly, yet the משנה did not mention it.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman disqualified from marrying a כֹּהֵן, such as the daughter of a forbidden priestly union
The child follows the father's status
'But there is...': an opening that brings a case to challenge a claim

phrases.english: But there is an Israelite who married a חללה,
where there is betrothal and there is no transgression,
and the child follows the male!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a new missing case after Step 7 dealt with the חלל and בת ישראל case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The completeness of the משנה's list of cases under the first rule
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An ישראל marrying a חללה meets all three conditions (קידושין, no עבירה, child follows father), so the list looks incomplete.

steps.title: The words 'any case' in the first clause include it
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's broad wording 'כל מקום' in its first clause covers the ישראל and חללה case.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said 'any case' in its first clause in order to include this one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה did cover this case, through its general wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first rule opens with 'כל מקום', any case where there is קידושין and no עבירה. That general phrase is what brings in the ישראל and חללה case, even though it is not in the list of examples.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Any case': broad wording that adds cases not named
The first clause of a משנה
To include

phrases.english: He taught "any case" in the first clause,
to include it.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The list of examples seemed to be the whole scope of the rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: The general phrase 'כל מקום' of the first clause covers the ישראל and חללה case.

steps.title: Why not state it outright?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה did not just list the ישראל and חללה case openly.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let the משנה teach it openly!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back: if the case belongs to the rule, why not name it directly?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Including a case only through general wording is a weaker way to teach it. If the case fits, the simpler choice would be to add it to the list of examples.

keyTerms.meaning: Then let him teach it
Openly, outright

phrases.english: But let him teach it explicitly!

steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the case is covered only by general wording
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the case fits the rule, it should have been listed openly with the other examples.

steps.title: The case does not fit into the list's sentence
steps.stepSummary: The משנה could not list it, because its sentence pairs each woman with a כהן, a לוי, and an ישראל, and a חללה may not marry a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: He did not list it because he could not. How would he say it? 'A כהנת, a לויה, an ישראלית, and a חללה who married a כהן, a לוי, or an ישראל'? But is a חללה fit for a כהן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the case could not be added to the משנה's list without making the sentence wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list is built as one sentence: these women who married any of these men. Adding a חללה to it would imply she may marry a כהן, which is forbidden and is an עבירה. So the משנה left her to the general phrase 'כל מקום'.

keyTerms.meaning: Because he cannot teach it
How would he teach it?
Is she fit?

phrases.english: Because he cannot teach it.
How would he teach it?
A daughter of a כהן, a לויה, an ישראלית, and a חללה
who married a כהן, a לוי, or an ישראל?
But is a חללה fit for a כהן?

steps.terutzResolutionType: Stylistic limitation of the משנה's sentence
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The case could simply have been added to the list.
steps.terutzMaskana: The list's structure pairs every woman with all three kinds of men, and a חללה cannot marry a כהן, so she could only be included through 'כל מקום'.

steps.title: The son of Egyptian converts is also missing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רבי יוחנן's ruling that the son of a second-generation מצרי and a first-generation מצרית counts as third generation. That is another case where the child follows the father, and it is not listed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is the ruling of רבה בר בר חנה in the name of רבי יוחנן: if a second-generation מצרי married a first-generation מצרית, her son counts as third generation!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the list again, this time with a case about Egyptian converts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מצרי convert's descendants may marry into the Jewish people only from the third generation. רבי יוחנן rules that the child follows the father: the father is second generation, so the son is third and is allowed. This is קידושין with no עבירה where the child follows the father, yet the משנה does not list it.

keyTerms.meaning: A second-generation Egyptian, the son of an Egyptian convert
A first-generation Egyptian woman, who converted herself
Third generation, who may marry into the Jewish people
'But there is...': brings a case that challenges a claim

phrases.english: But there is the ruling of רבה בר בר חנה,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: as רבה בר בר חנה said that רבי יוחנן said:
A second-generation Egyptian man who married a first-generation Egyptian woman,
phrases.notes: The rule that an Egyptian may join only from the third generation is from דברים 23:9.

phrases.english: her son is third-generation!
phrases.notes: The son follows his father's count, so he is fully allowed to marry into the Jewish people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ישראל and חללה case was resolved, brings a new missing case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The completeness of the משנה's list of cases under the first rule
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The son of a מצרי שני and a מצרית ראשונה follows the father in a valid marriage with no עבירה, yet he is not listed.

steps.title: 'Any case' includes the Egyptian case too
steps.stepSummary: Following רבי יוחנן, the general wording 'כל מקום' in the first clause covers the Egyptian case.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said 'any case' in its first clause in order to include this one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same answer as before: the broad wording includes this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as with the חללה, the משנה did not need to list the Egyptian case by name. The opening phrase 'כל מקום' already brings it in.

phrases.english: He taught "any case" in the first clause,
to include it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 12 the same way Step 9 answered Step 8.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The Egyptian case seemed to be left out of the rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'כל מקום' covers it, in line with רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: For רב דימי, 'which is this' leaves the case out
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי holds that the son is only second generation. For him, the words 'ואיזו זו' limit the rule, so the Egyptian case is excluded.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רב דימי, who says the son counts as second generation, the משנה said 'which is this' in order to exclude this case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer that fits רב דימי, who disagrees with the ruling רבה בר בר חנה reported.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב דימי the son does not follow the father here, so he is still second generation and may not marry into the Jewish people. That means the case does not belong under the first rule at all. The words 'ואיזו זו' limit the rule to the listed examples, which shuts this case out.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Which is this': limiting wording that introduces the list
To exclude

steps.whatToRemember: The general phrase 'כל מקום' brings in cases that were not named, while 'ואיזו זו' can limit the rule to the listed ones. Which phrase does the work depends on which opinion the case follows.

phrases.english: And according to רב דימי, who said he is second-generation,
he taught "which is this" to exclude it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a parallel answer to Step 12 according to רב דימי, whose ruling differs from רבה בר בר חנה's report.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting wording excludes the case under a dissenting opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The Egyptian case would need to be included in the first rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רב דימי the son is second generation, and 'ואיזו זו' excludes the case from the rule.

steps.title: רבין's report about converts from two nations
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רבין's report of רבי יוחנן's ruling. Among non-Jews the child follows the father. Once they convert, the child follows whichever parent has the flawed lineage. This seems to clash with the משנה's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is a case that does not fit. When רבין came, he said that רבי יוחנן said: among the nations, follow the male. If they converted, follow the one of the two who has the flawed lineage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more case where the משנה's rule seems not to work. These converts may marry each other and do no sin, yet the child does not follow the father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that when the marriage takes effect and there is no sin, the child follows the father. For converts from two different nations, רבי יוחנן says the child follows the flawed parent, even if that parent is the mother. So this is a case that fits the משנה's conditions but gives a different result.

keyTerms.meaning: The nations; here, non-Jews from different peoples
Follow the male: the child gets the father's status
They converted to Judaism
Flawed; the parent with the lower or blemished lineage

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two halves. As non-Jews, the child follows the father. Only after they convert does the child follow the flawed parent. The problem for the משנה comes from the second half.

phrases.english: But there is [this case]:
for when רבין came
he said that רבי יוחנן said:
Among the nations, follow the male.
phrases.notes: He means two non-Jews from different nations who married each other.

phrases.english: If they converted,
follow the flawed one of the two of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the Egyptian case of רב דימי was handled, the גמרא brings a second case in the same pattern.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that when the marriage takes effect and there is no sin, the child follows the male
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Converts from two nations may marry with no sin, yet רבי יוחנן says the child follows the flawed parent. So the משנה should have mentioned this exception.

steps.title: The words 'which case is this' exclude רבין's case
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's words 'ואיזו זו' limit the rule, and they exclude רבין's case of converts.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה taught 'which case is this' in order to exclude this case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה did hint at this case. Its words 'ואיזו זו' are there to leave this case out of the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same kind of answer that was given for רב דימי in step 14. The phrase 'ואיזו זו' narrows the rule to the specific examples the משנה lists. Cases like converts from two nations fall outside it.

keyTerms.meaning: It taught; here, the משנה wrote these words on purpose
'Which case is this': the משנה's phrase that narrows the rule to its listed examples
To exclude; to leave a case out of the rule

phrases.english: [The משנה] taught 'which case is this' to exclude [it].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רבין's report in step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading a word in the משנה as excluding the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the converts may marry without sin, you might think their child is covered by the 'follow the male' rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'איזו זו' limits the rule, so the case of converts from two nations is excluded.

steps.title: Questioning the claim that the משנה follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the claim that the משנה follows רבי יוסי. It shows that if the משנה follows רבי יהודה, every word fits neatly. 'כל מקום' includes ישראל with a חללה and the Egyptian ruling of רבה בר בר חנה. 'איזו זו' excludes the rulings of רב דימי and רבין.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is this claim? It works well if you say the משנה follows רבי יהודה. Then 'any case' in the first clause comes to include a ישראל who married a חללה, and also the ruling of רבה בר בר חנה. And 'which case is this' comes to exclude the rulings of רב דימי and רבין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns back to an earlier claim, that the משנה follows רבי יוסי, and asks how that can be. It lays out how neatly the משנה fits רבי יהודה, which prepares the next move: following רבי יוסי does not fit as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה follows רבי יהודה, the extra words have clear jobs. 'כל מקום' adds two cases where the child follows the father: ישראל with a חללה, and the third-generation Egyptian of רבה בר בר חנה. 'איזו זו' removes the two cases where the child does not follow the father: רב דימי and רבין. The words 'אי אמרת בשלמא' ('granted, if you say') hint that the רבי יוסי reading has no such neat fit.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What is this?': a sharp way of questioning a claim just made
'Granted, if you say': this works fine under one view, which suggests the other view has a problem
'Any case': the general opening words of the משנה's first clause
The first clause of the משנה
To include; to bring in an extra case

steps.whatToRemember: Under רבי יהודה, the משנה's extra words fit neatly: 'כל מקום' includes ישראל with a חללה and רבה בר בר חנה's Egyptian case, and 'איזו זו' excludes רב דימי and רבין. This makes the earlier claim that the משנה follows רבי יוסי look weaker.
steps.confusionAlert: 'כל מקום' and 'איזו זו' work in opposite directions. 'כל מקום' adds cases to the rule, and 'איזו זו' takes cases out of it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This step reopens the question of which תנא the משנה follows. It uses the job of each extra word as the test.

phrases.english: What is this?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is going back to the earlier claim that the משנה follows רבי יוסי.

phrases.english: Granted, if you say
[that] our משנה is רבי יהודה,
'any case' of the first clause
[comes] to include a ישראל who married a חללה,
and [the ruling] of רבה בר בר חנה,
phrases.notes: This is the Egyptian ruling from step 12: the son counts as third generation.

phrases.english: [and] 'which case is this' [comes] to exclude
[the rulings] of רב דימי and רבין!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי מַאי? אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא מַתְנִיתִין רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to step 5's claim that the משנה follows רבי יוסי. It uses the word-jobs worked out in steps 9, 13, 14 and 16 to show how neatly the רבי יהודה reading from step 2 fits.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier claim that the משנה follows רבי יוסי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under רבי יהודה, every extra word has a clear job: two cases included and two excluded. The 'granted' wording suggests that under רבי יוסי this neat fit is lost.
